title: Rishabh Pant Seeks Uttarakhand CM's Help to Buy Land, Build First Home in Native State
excerpt: India cricketer made a late-night appeal on X to CM Pushkar Singh Dhami, saying he wants to move back from Delhi and buy land at government rates. Dhami responded with assurance of full support.
body:
• Rishabh Pant posted a late-night appeal on X to Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami, seeking help to buy land in his home state
  • The India wicketkeeper-batter wants to move his base from Delhi to Uttarakhand and build his first home there, after paying ₹28.34 crore in taxes
  • CM Dhami responded positively, directing officials to contact Pant and assist with the land acquisition process within existing regulations

India cricketer Rishabh Pant has turned to Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami with an unusual request — help buying land in his native state so he can build his first home there.

Pant, who was born in Roorkee in the Haridwar district and is Uttarakhand's official brand ambassador, made the appeal via a late-night post on X. The wicketkeeper-batter said he wants to shift his base from Delhi back to Uttarakhand, where his family has deep roots, and purchase land at official government rates.

The Appeal

In his post, which quickly went viral, Pant noted he had paid ₹28.34 crore in taxes and quipped that "a gift would be lovely" — an apparent light-hearted nudge at the state government to consider gifting land to the cricketer who has put Uttarakhand on the global sports map.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=WZO1L3TNJFU

The 28-year-old, who became the most expensive player in Indian Premier League history when he was bought for ₹27 crore by the Lucknow Super Giants in the 2025 auction, framed the request as a matter of returning home. Pant has properties in Roorkee, Dehradun, Haridwar, and Delhi, but spends most of his time in the capital.

"A gift would be lovely, but I'm happy to buy land at government rates. I just want to build my first home in my state."

— Rishabh Pant, in his X post

Why It's Not Simple

Buying land in Uttarakhand, even for native-born residents, is not straightforward. The state enacted stringent land regulations in 2025, banning outsiders from purchasing agricultural and horticultural land in 11 of its 13 districts, with only Haridwar and Udham Singh Nagar exempted. Non-residents are limited to 250 square metres of residential land.

While Pant is a native of Uttarakhand — born and raised in Roorkee — his official residency in Delhi could complicate matters under the strict interpretation of the state's land laws. The regulations were introduced by CM Dhami's government to curb large-scale land purchases by outsiders that had triggered protests from local communities worried about demographic shifts and rising land prices in hill districts.

CM Dhami's Response

Dhami responded promptly to Pant's appeal. The Chief Minister assured the cricketer that the state government would provide full support within the framework of existing rules and directed officials to contact Pant and guide him through the land acquisition process.

The exchange underscores the broader complexity of land ownership in Uttarakhand, where even high-profile natives can find the bureaucratic process daunting. Pant's public appeal — and the CM's quick response — also highlights the political significance of the state's land laws ahead of the 2027 Uttarakhand assembly elections, with the BJP signaling CM Dhami as its face for the contest.

Pant and Uttarakhand

Pant has long been connected to his home state. He was appointed Uttarakhand's brand ambassador by Dhami in 2021, with the CM citing the cricketer's rise from modest beginnings in Roorkee as an inspiration for the state's youth. During his devastating car accident on the Delhi-Dehradun highway in December 2022, Dhami personally visited Pant at the hospital and promised state support for his treatment.

The cricketer also donated his match fee to Uttarakhand flood relief efforts in 2021. His desire to build a home in the state marks another personal chapter — one that lands squarely in the middle of a live political debate about who can own land in the Himalayan state.
